verdict: Nu grew IFRS revenue 57% in dollars to $4.7B and profit 62% to a record $895M, closing 2025 with 131 million customers and a 33% return on equity.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: Total revenue $4.7B vs $3.0B in Q4 2024, in dollars (IFRS accounting basis)

kpis.label: Net income
kpis.note: A record high, up 62% in dollars from $553M a year ago; return on equity was 33%

kpis.label: Customers
kpis.note: 131 million total, up 15% from 114.2 million a year ago; 4 million added in the quarter

kpis.label: Deposits
kpis.note: Customer deposits held with Nu, up 29% year over year; credit portfolio $32.7B, up 40%

segments.name: Interest income & instrument gains
segments.note: Interest earned on loans, credit cards and investments, plus gains on financial instruments — the core money a bank makes from lending. In the accounting P&L this is credit income of $2,732.0M plus float (treasury) income of $1,264.3M.

segments.name: Fee and commission income
segments.note: Fees and commissions from cards and other services customers use in the app.

opex.name: Customer support and operations
opex.note: Customer support and day-to-day operations for an app-only bank with no branches.

opex.name: General and administrative expenses
opex.note: Staff, technology and running the company — the biggest operating cost block.

opex.name: Other expenses
opex.note: Other operating expenses as reported in the accounting P&L.

takeaways.title: A record profit, at a 33% ROE
takeaways.text: Net income reached $894.8M, up 62% in dollars from $552.6M a year ago, for a record 33% return on equity. Full-year net income was $2.9B, up from $2.0B in 2024.

takeaways.title: 17 million customers added in 2025
takeaways.text: Nu added 4 million customers in the quarter to reach 131 million — 113 million in Brazil, where it is now the largest private financial institution by customer count, about 15% of Mexico's adult population, and over 4 million in Colombia. Monthly revenue per active customer reached $15.

takeaways.title: Credit quality improved at year-end
takeaways.text: The 15–90 day delinquency ratio fell to 4.1% and the 90+ ratio to 6.6%, helped by Brazil's 13th-salary seasonality, while the credit portfolio grew 40% to $32.7B and deposits rose 29% to $41.9B.

oneTimers: This was the first quarter reported under Nu's new Managerial P&L framework. This page uses the IFRS accounting P&L from the KPMG-assured reconciliation bridge: managerial revenue was $4,857.3M, but net income is identical ($894.8M) on both bases.
Risk-adjusted NIM of 10.5% included a one-off extraordinary contribution to Prosofipo, the sector-wide deposit-protection fund all Mexican Sofipos must fund.
In January 2026 Nu received conditional OCC approval for a U.S. national bank charter — the first of three clearances for its planned U.S. expansion.
otherDetail: A $0.4M share of losses from associates — the accounting P&L has no separate other-income line this quarter.
footerNote: Nu is a digital bank; cost of revenue is mostly interest paid to depositors and loan-loss provisions. Figures are the IFRS accounting P&L from the reconciliation bridge; its rounded components sum to $4,685.8M against the $4,685.9M total shown in the filing.
